summary:
The service started this run, not an instruction: the f* 0.33 nudge loop (Hatteras job 164655) had ended. There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered as asked, and no time went to unasked work. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claim is open on this line. The run answered all three points of my earlier Nov 24 review. It stated plainly that E0089's loop-completion clause has failed at f* 0.33 and 0.57, which holds. It wrote a per-run budget guard (D0072), and its arithmetic holds. And it corrected the 'five times' cross-machine comparison, but that correction is itself wrong, for the reason below, and so was the figure my earlier review gave.

Main finding: every per-step collision count in the E0089 tables is a running total for the whole loop, not a count for that step. tools/ramp.py builds each step's starting checkpoint by copying the previous step's checkpoint and resetting only the cycle number and Gamma. The engine's save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint (granular/sim.py on method/nudge, lines 331 to 362) store and restore the counters (cnt) and energy terms (en). So counters.json, and the referee's own events_per_particle_cycle in summary.json (referee/long_contact.py line 187, which divides sim.cnt by the step's cycles), add up every step since the loop began. The mirror shows it directly: total events after steps 0, 1 and 2 of the f* 0.33 loop are 0.58, 0.88 and 1.19 billion, rising steadily. The energy audit is not affected, because it works from changes over each chunk (en0 and cnt0, long_contact.py line 255). The CPU-seconds figures are per step and are right.

I recomputed both ended loops from the differences between consecutive steps' counters.json files (all fourteen f* 0.33 files match their recorded SHA-256 and sizes). The corrected figures are below; the run's figures are in brackets.
f* 0.33, collisions per particle per cycle: 1,778 at 4.5, 6,201 at 4.55 and 37,569 at 4.6 [13,967, 20,168, 61,579].
f* 0.33, plate collisions per particle per cycle: 411, 1,069 and 4,535 [1,336, 2,405, 7,398].
f* 0.57, collisions per particle per cycle: 1,351, 4,378 and 33,296 [12,756, 17,133, 51,918].
f* 0.57, plate collisions: 366, 977 and 5,223 [1,319, 2,297, 7,720].

What follows from the corrected figures:
(a) From 4.5 to 4.55, collisions per cycle rose 3.5 times at f* 0.33 and 3.2 times at f* 0.57, not 1.44 and 1.34 times. Most of the 'five times' CPU rise was real. The machine accounts for only about 1.6 times: about 2.2 to 2.3 microseconds per collision on the Mac at 4.5, against 3.6 to 3.7 on Hatteras at 4.55. My earlier review's 'Hatteras is roughly two times slower', which the run adopted, used the same running totals and was also wrong.
(b) From 4.55 to 4.6 on Hatteras, collisions per cycle rose 6.1 times at f* 0.33 and 7.6 times at f* 0.57. CPU per collision barely changed: 3.58 to 3.65 microseconds and 3.73 to 3.76, ratios of 1.02 and 1.01. So the second proposed direction, to find out why CPU per collision grows 2 to 2.5 times at 4.6, is chasing an artifact of the running totals. The wall is extra collisions, not slower collisions.
(c) Plate collisions per particle per cycle at 4.6 are 11 times their 4.5 level at f* 0.33 and 14 times at f* 0.57. They are not 'about 5.5 times'.
(d) The ball-model and wall analyses on this line may carry the same error. evidence/E0085-nudge-wall-fields.json uses events_per_particle_cycle, as may E0065 and E0088, and so may other lines that use tools/ramp.py. I did not recheck those.

The line state for L0015 (nudge fast pass), as written in this run, has wrong sentences. 'with plate collisions per cycle about 5.5 times those at 4.5' should read about 11 to 14 times. In the line note, 'in events it is 1.34 times' should read about 3.2 times (3.5 at f* 0.33). The state's other sentences hold: two of eight loops ended at Gamma 4.6 on the 48 CPU-hour cap, the completion clause failed at both, the cost-drop prediction is untested, and six loops are still running. What would resolve this, in one session: rebuild evidence/E0089-interim-f0.33.json and -f0.57.json from step-to-step differences. For the first Hatteras step, subtract the counters of the input checkpoint's step. Correct the ratios, the line note and state, and PROGRAM.md. Withdraw the CPU-per-collision direction. Check E0065, E0085 and E0088 for the same error. Tell Chris that the referee's events_per_particle_cycle is a loop running total whenever ramp.py starts a step from a copied checkpoint. That file is Chris's, not the agent's to change.

Smaller points. The summary lists B0008 as open and says it 'would stop any new nudge job being submitted from here'. But B0008 was resolved at 06:12Z today: method/nudge is in this clone at 16f3334, and I confirmed it. The D0072 guard depends on a service timer for Nov 26 08:00Z. I could not find the timer database from here, so I could not confirm the timer exists. If it doesn't, nothing enforces the 100 CPU-hour limit for a loop that gets past 4.6. The guard's arithmetic is right: each job runs on one CPU, so none can reach 100 CPU-hours before 100 wall-hours after it started, which is Nov 26 at about 09:27Z. This run's ledger timestamps (15:07:28Z and 15:08:09Z) come before its recorded end and its commit, which fixes the written-ahead pattern I reported last time.

Housekeeping. program check passes. It lists approvals on Nov 23 at 15:47 and 15:49 and on Nov 24 at 03:19, which Chris should confirm were Chris's. While I worked, it failed once because of my own scratch folder sequel-data/checker/, which CHECKER.md tells the checker to use. I deleted the folder, and the check passed again. sequel-data is 647 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling, free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor, tmp/ is empty, and active.jsonl is empty. The only recent files outside the two allowed folders belong to the harness. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0015 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a six-minute service run. Job 164655 ended at 15:01:36Z, and the service recorded it at 15:02:28Z. The run started at 15:03:35Z and ended at 15:09:50Z, with its commit one second later. It only read mirrored outputs, so zero local CPU-hours is right. The job's own 57.49 CPU-hours match its job record. It did what one ended job allows: it collected the loop, tabulated it, and answered the earlier review. Six E0089 loops are still running on Hatteras, waiting on their 48 CPU-hour step caps. None was started or cancelled. The host is Linux, so pmset and uptime are unavailable, and the summary says so. Free disk of 91 gigabytes matches. The machine did not limit the science; the registered step cap did.
discrepancies: open_blockers lists B0008, and limits_hit says it would stop new nudge jobs from here. B0008 was resolved at 2026-11-24T06:12Z, and method/nudge is present in this clone at 16f3334.
The Nov 26 08:00Z wake that D0072 relies on could not be confirmed from this machine. The service's timer database was not found.
